messages:
incidents-bot: [PAGER] HIGH GPU QUEUE GROWTH detected for cluster: eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3
incidents-bot: symptom="queue_length > 3000 and tail_latency_95 > 1200ms" severity=sev2 runbook=https://redwood.runbooks/gpu-queue
incidents-bot: autoscaler status: reached_max_replicas (24) | recent_scale_events: 6 in 10m | metric: kv_cache_bytes_per_gpu increasing rapidly

sre_oncall_maya: taking this. paging in eng-runtime and ml-ops. @eng-runtime-jonas @ml-ops-rosalind can you join? :rotating_light:

eng-runtime-jonas: joining. seeing massive prefill/warmup traffic to model v24.3 since rollout 00:12 UTC. Initial hypothesis: v24.3 increased kv-cache footprint and triggered large prefetches that amplified token count per request.

ml-ops-rosalind: confirmed. Canary logs show host-level KV entries growing ~4x on first 50 requests after coldstart. Also noticed higher average context length in histograms.

sre_oncall_maya: posting quick metrics snapshot:

```
queue_length: 3124 -> 4278 (30m)
gpu_util_avg: 92% -> 98%
autoscaler_replicas: 24 (max)
model_version: v24.3 rolled to 40% traffic @ 00:10 UTC
tail_95_latency_ms: 1200 -> 2500
error_rate_5xx: 0.7% -> 8.1% (timeouts & throttles)
```

platform-tim: autoscaler hit cloud quota for GPUs in eu-west-1, request to cloud for quota bump is in flight (ticket #CLOUD-1829). ETA uncertain.

eng-runtime-jonas: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) pause the v24.3 rollout 2) route new requests away from eu-west-1 pool 3) apply temporary per-request token limit and disable prefill/warmup on v24.3 4) fallback traffic to v24.2. Which do we want now?

sre_oncall_maya: do 1, 3, 4 now. We'll also open a manual reserved pool to absorb some burst if possible. @ deploy-bot kick off pinned-instance spin up for gp2-reserved-pool?

deploy-bot: acknowledged. Starting reserved pool provisioning job: job_id=prov-9876. Estimated spin-up ~ 8-12 min.

ml-ops-rosalind: executing hotfix to disable prefetch on v24.3 now. Patch applied to canaries, rolling to replicas but paused at global rollout. Config snippet applied:

```
model.v24.3.warmup.enabled=false
model.v24.3.prefetch.batch_size=0
request.max_tokens_per_call=1024  # temporary
```

eng-runtime-jonas: also updated routing policy to send new sessions for critical customers to v24.2 in eu-west-1. Non-critical sessions still land on v24.3 but with warmup disabled.

cs-lucas: quick customer impact snapshot: approximately 27 customers saw elevated latency, 5 customers hit degraded throughput impacting API SLAs. Top impacted: devx-beta, search-inc, docuflow. Notifying their CS leads and drafting status note.

pm-anya: prioritizing top 5 customers for proactive outreach. Can SRE provide ETA to recovery?

sre_oncall_maya: after hotfix + pause rollout, queue started to trend down in the last 4m. Current queue: 2340, tail_95: 1600ms. Reserved pool provisioning still in progress. If reserved pool completes and we can re-route ~30% of traffic, we should be under pressure in ~10-15m.

eng-runtime-jonas: got a suspicious log line in the warmup path that explains 1 request causing a cascade of prefetch calls:

```
2026-03-15T00:11:34Z v24.3 warmup: prefetch_keys=8192 user_ctx_tokens=20480 prefetch_estimated_mem=3.6GB
```

eng-runtime-jonas: That's far above the usual prefetch. Looks like tokenizer or prompt template changed in v24.3 causing inferred context length inflation for some requests.

ml-ops-rosalind: rolling back tokenizer patch in v24.3 commit chain to earlier commit (reverted commit abc123). But we won't roll back full model yet; prefer to keep paused and run tests.

platform-tim: cloud quota bumped request approved? Update: support email says we have soft capacity available in another AZ; we can spin up cross-AZ pool but network egress will increase latency for some sessions. Worth it?

sre_oncall_maya: yes, spin up cross-AZ reserved nodes and drain low-priority queues onto them. Engage network team for routing.

deploy-bot: reserved pool prov-9876 completed. New nodes: 6 gpus added (cross-az).

eng-runtime-jonas: rebalanced incoming weight: eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3 -> -20% weight, eu-west-1-gpu-pool-aux -> +20% (cross-az). Now queuing drops to ~900. CPU/GPU memory stays high but stable.

cs-lucas: updating customers: initial status note sent to top 5, telling them we are mitigating, expected partial recovery in 15-30m.

pm-anya: good, prepare a follow-up note after 1 hour with root cause summary and next steps.

sre_oncall_maya: action list for now:
- pause v24.3 rollout (done)
- disable warmup/prefetch on v24.3 (done)
- revert tokenizer change in v24.3 (in flight)
- provisioned reserved pool + cross-AZ routing (done)
- cloud quota follow-up with infra (tim)
- customer comms (cs)

eng-runtime-jonas: adding a throttling safeguard to the runtime to cap prefetch keys per request to 1024 as a protective measure. Patch pushed to canaries.

ml-ops-rosalind: running a targeted test suite on v24.3 with representative prompts; if warmup behavior looks ok after tokenizer revert, we can consider a cautious resume to <5% traffic with warmup disabled and strict prefetch caps.

sre_oncall_maya: root cause emerging: accidental tokenizer change + model warmup aggressiveness in v24.3 caused per-request prefetch explosion -> kv-cache blowout -> autoscaler hit max -> queue spiral. We'll treat as regression introduced by rollout.

platform-tim: follow-up: cloud ticket CLOUD-1829 resolved with temporary quota increase; downstream action to request permanent capacity increase or improved autoscaler fallback.

pm-anya: tagging this incident for postmortem. PM/ML/Runtime to co-own action items: safer warmup defaults, rollout canary thresholds based on kv_cache growth, add autoscaler soft-limit fallback (route to different model) and customer-impact dashboard.

cs-lucas: CS will prepare customer impact list + timelines for outreach. Expecting to send consolidated update in ~45m.

eng-runtime-jonas: quick snippet of the mitigation commands used (for runbook update):

```
# pause rollout
redwoodctl rollout pause model:v24.3 --env=prod

# disable warmup flag
redwoodctl config set model:v24.3 warmup.enabled=false

# cap prefetch
redwoodctl config set runtime.prefetch.max_keys=1024

# reweight routing
redwoodctl traffic route set model:v24.2=80% model:v24.3=20% --region=eu-west-1
```

sre_oncall_maya: monitoring continues. current queue 420, tail_95 480ms, error_rate 1.2%. Will keep this thread open until fully stable and customer comms dispatched.

deploy-bot: automated deploys for v24.3 warmup flag are paused until manual approval.

eng-runtime-jonas: suggested postmortem items: add metric alert for kv_cache_bytes_per_request ratio, introduce canary test that measures per-request prefetch_keys distribution, and require explicit opt-in for tokenizer changes in rollouts.

ml-ops-rosalind: agreed. Also recommend adding a rollout safety valve that drops warmup for new model versions automatically if prefetch rates exceed threshold.

sre_oncall_maya: handoff: I'll keep monitoring for next hour then hand to night oncall if stable. If queue stays <500 and tail_95 <600ms for 30m, we'll close.

pm-anya: thanks all. Action owners: runtime (jonas) - safety caps + runbook update; ml-ops (rosalind) - tokenizer revert verification + small canary run; platform (tim) - follow cloud quota/perm capacity; cs (lucas) - customer comms.

cs-lucas: posting initial status note to affected customers now.

sre_oncall_maya: updating incident channel: incident_state=mitigated | mitigations_applied=[pause_rollout, disable_warmup, reserved_pool, prefetch_cap] | next_steps=postmortem + permanent fixes

sre_oncall_maya: closing note: queue stable at 210, tail_95 380ms, error_rate 0.4%. Will transition monitoring to runbook checks. If anyone sees new anomalies tag me. :white_check_mark:
